requirement: When implementation shows that agreed requirement text must change, the `habeas-requirements` skill MUST direct agents to stop work that depends on the change and take the changed requirements through review, agreement, and commit before continuing.
rationale:
The requirement has two obligations for the `habeas-requirements` skill. When implementation shows agreed text must change, it must tell agents to stop work that depends on the change. It must also tell them to take the changed requirements through review, agreement and commit before continuing.

One marked test, `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[the_requirements_skill_stops_dependent_work_when_agreed_text_must_change]`, covers both.

- **Stop work and go through review first:** The test uses `assert_phrases` to assert that the collapsed bundled skill contains the sentence "If implementation shows that agreed text must change, stop work that depends on it and take the changed requirements through steps 3 to 5 first". The helper collapses whitespace, so the skill's line wrapping doesn't matter. The assertion covers the trigger (implementation shows agreed text must change). It covers "stop work that depends on it". It covers the changed requirements going through the steps, and "first" supplies the "before continuing" ordering.
- **Steps 3 to 5 are review, agreement and commit:** The test also asserts through `step("habeas-requirements", n)` that step 3 starts with "Review.", step 4 with "Present" and step 5 with "Commit.". I read `assets/skills/habeas-requirements/SKILL.md#section[Habeas requirements]/section[Workflow]` to check this. Step 3 is the subagent review. Step 4 presents each group to the user and has a gate until the user agrees, rejects or defers it. Step 5 commits. So the referenced steps really are review, agreement and commit. If someone renumbered the steps without updating the sentence, the test would fail.

The requirement is about skill text, so asserting on that text is the right way to verify it. Nothing else in the requirement needs its own test.
